title: Boars and Their Habitats
summary: Dur the dwarf's tongue-in-cheek travel bestiary: 31 tameable boar varieties of Classic Era, four unusual encounters, rare coats, hunter abilities and useful notes from beside the cooking pot.
changelog: First English edition, translated from the fourth Russian edition.
contentNotice: Facts checked against Classic Era references.

chapters.title: A Word Before We Begin: Who Ate the Map?

blocks.text: My name is Dur Blackbeard. I am a dwarf, a traveler, and a man of my word—the last part should not be taken too literally. Once, in Kharanos, I claimed I could identify any boar by its grunt. A minute later, the innkeeper threw me out into the yard. Turns out I was the one doing the grunting. So I took up proper observation instead.

And so began my journey, from the snows of Dun Morogh to lands where even the mud looks unwell. I recorded coats, habits, and ways to make friends. Recipes, too: a naturalist ought to know his subject from every angle, though I draw the line at putting my own companion in the stewpot.

blocks.alt: A black boar roots through an open travel pack; an apple and the corner of a map peek out.
blocks.caption: At our first meeting, he studied my baggage. I studied his character.

blocks.text: Collected here are thirty-one tameable varieties and four unusual encounters. I have left the quilboar out of the count: if a creature walks on two legs and demands a toll, that is a political matter. The numbers beside each beast are hunter’s notes on its level, not its age in winters. The ranks of Charge refer to the ability a tamed companion can learn.

The first illustration in this book was drawn by Mira Copperbraid, my friend and a cartographer from Ironforge. While I was writing this foreword, she managed to draw both me and the thief rummaging through my pack. The remaining sketches are my own. Mira can draw. I can usually tell what she has drawn. Usually.

blocks.alt: Dur, his black beard braided, makes notes in the snows of Dun Morogh while a boar investigates his travel pack.
blocks.caption: Illustration by Mira Copperbraid. The first rule of field notes: never keep your map beside the apples.

blocks.text: Here, the boars are black, the snow is white, and the reason a dwarf falls over is usually clear and smells of ale. All five varieties found here can be tamed, and all know Charge, Rank 1.
Small Crag Boar

Level 3. Black bristles, a small body, and an enormous opinion of itself. A handy choice for hunters who favor an understated local coat: you needn’t travel to the edge of the world to find a black boar.
Crag Boar

Levels 5–6. The same dark coat, but with tusks that mean business. Crag Boars yield special ribs used in Ragnar Thunderbrew’s dish. Don’t try passing off ordinary ribs from elsewhere in their place. The brewer can tell them apart better than I can tell my relatives.

blocks.alt: A large black crag boar gently nudges a piglet; a pine sprig lies nearby.
blocks.caption: Stubbornness is inherited long before the tusks come in.

blocks.text: Large Crag Boar

Levels 6–7, black-coated. This is the beast on which dwarf hunters begin their first taming trial with Grif Wildheart. The word “large” also applies to the bruise you may earn as part of your training.
Elder Crag Boar

Levels 7–8. Its color is almost indistinguishable from that of the younger stock. Don’t expect the word “old” to grant it Charge, Rank 2: life experience and a hunter’s training are counted separately.
Scarred Crag Boar

Levels 9–10. Its pale, almost ivory coat sets it apart from its black neighbors. A good local choice if you’d like a light-colored companion. The scars look impressive, but they won’t provide leatherworkers with some miraculous special hide.

chapters.title: Loch Modan: A Lake, Mountains, and Three Temperaments

blocks.text: Beyond the pass, I met boars who recognized only two roads: the one leading to food, and the one leading straight through my camp. All three varieties can be tamed; here, you can also find Charge, Rank 2.
Mountain Boar

Levels 10–11, brown-coated, with Charge, Rank 1. A reliable choice for anyone who favors an earthy hue. Ribs from local Mountain Boars are useful to cooks; just don’t confuse them with the special Crag Boar ribs from Dun Morogh.
Mangy Mountain Boar

Levels 14–15, reddish in color, with Charge, Rank 2. Its name is insulting, but its lessons are useful. It was the first to teach me that a battered appearance does not necessarily mean a poor charge.
Elder Mountain Boar

Levels 16–17, brown-coated, with the same second rank. It differs from its younger mountain kin chiefly in level and the ability it can teach. I called it Professor in my journal. The Professor ate the corner of my diploma.

blocks.alt: Three sketches of common boar coats: black, brown, and pale, with cloven hoofprints beside them.
blocks.caption: It’s easier to remember a coat by looking at the beast. The beast will find the mud on its own.

chapters.title: Elwynn Forest: At the Princess’s Court

blocks.text: Here, boars have been taxing farmers without a single royal decree. All five entries from this region are tameable beasts with Charge, Rank 1.
Stonetusk Boar
A pale inhabitant of the farmlands. Its meat is useful to novice cooks: a simple cut, fit for roasting without elaborate seasoning. Taming one, of course, leaves you with a companion—not supper.
Rockhide Boar

Levels 7–8, pale-coated. The name promises armor, but once tamed, it grants no special advantage merely by virtue of its title. I could call myself Impenetrable; the cobbler who has seen my trousers would disagree.
Princess

Level 9, golden-coated. Her court is the pumpkin patch of the Brackwell farm; her subjects are the trampled rows. She can be tamed. But if you’re carrying out the assignment to put an end to her reign, you’ll need a collar: a living companion in the stable won’t do the job for you.

blocks.alt: The golden-coated Princess stands beside a half-eaten pumpkin and a broken fence, wearing a simple collar.
blocks.caption: Her Highness has requested seconds.

blocks.text: Porcine Entourage

Level 7, brown-coated. It accompanies Princess and makes a quiet audience with Her Highness rather difficult. Deal with her entourage first: no one forms a polite queue of boars while you’re trying to tame one.
Longsnout

Levels 10–11, black-coated. Another Elwynn option for hunters who like dark bristles. A special name does not make it a rare beast like Grunter. I checked: a long nose won’t get you a discount from the merchants, either.

chapters.title: Westfall and Redridge: A Four-Legged Pie

blocks.text: At the sight of the local fields, I reached for my sketchbook. At the sight of the boars, I reached for my recipe journal. I waited until they looked away, then reached for my sketchbook again.
Young Goretusk

Levels 12–13, golden-coated, found in Westfall. Older notes sometimes call it a Young Bloodsnout. It can be tamed and teaches Charge, Rank 2. Young local beasts provide livers for pies and snouts for stew.
Goretusk

Levels 14–15, reddish, found in Westfall; another familiar name is Bloodsnout. It can also be tamed and teaches Rank 2. Its liver and ribs make it useful to cooks, but I kept my recipes well away from the feeding trough. There was no need to sour the friendship.

blocks.alt: A red and a golden boar; a half-eaten pumpkin lies beside the golden one, with tusks sketched in the margins.
blocks.caption: A royal coat does not excuse one from charges of pumpkin vandalism.

blocks.text: Great Goretusk

Levels 16–17, red-coated. Look in southeastern Westfall and western Redridge. It can be tamed and teaches Charge, Rank 2. Its large snout is needed for a Redridge goulash quest. Don’t confuse a quest’s shopping list with a learned cooking recipe: they don’t call for the same ingredients.
Bellygrub

Level 24, brown-coated, found near Lakeshire in Redridge. It wrecks Martie Jainrose’s garden and can be tamed to learn Charge, Rank 3. Here’s a ground-level trainer that doesn’t require a trip into a dungeon. The landlady needs its tusk for her errand; befriending the garden bandit won’t impress her.

chapters.title: Teldrassil: Beneath the Great Tree’s Roots

blocks.text: The night elves spent a long time explaining the balance of nature to me. I listened carefully until a boar made off with my midday meal. After that, the balance of nature required a second lunch.
Young Thistle Boar

Levels 1–2, golden-coated. Found in Teldrassil’s starting lands, it can be tamed and knows Charge, Rank 1. It may look modest, but it can become a full-fledged companion. A beast’s low level does not excuse a hunter from first learning how to tame it.

blocks.alt: A young golden and a reddish strigid boar sniff a large fallen leaf; a fern grows nearby.
blocks.caption: The elf called it contemplation. The boar would have called it a snack.

blocks.text: Thistle Boar

Levels 2–3, reddish. Another tameable bearer of Rank 1. That means you can choose between two different coats on a single island without mounting an expedition across half the world. Someone told me that after I’d already paid for the ship.

Both fall under the local keepers’ concerns about nature’s balance. But don’t credit them with enchanted elven ribs: being born beneath the Great Tree does not turn ordinary meat into a rare delicacy.

chapters.title: Durotar: Dust in the Beard, Spots on the Flanks

blocks.text: A large boulder helped me observe the local beasts. It concealed the orcs from me less effectively than it concealed me from the orcs, but that shortcoming falls outside the scope of a book about boars. All four varieties can be tamed and know Charge, Rank 1.
Mottled Boar

Levels 1–2, pale-coated, found around the Valley of Trials. The earliest local specimen. The name “mottled” does not promise a special pattern after taming: judge the beast itself, not the eloquence of whoever compiled the list.
Dire Mottled Boar
Levels 6–7, black-coated. Now that is a noticeable change in color from the first. For hunters, it’s a way to get a dark boar in Durotar without a stroll through the dwarf’s snowdrifts.

blocks.alt: A pale boar examines a small cactus while its black companion watches from behind.
blocks.caption: The cactus proved to be the only conversationalist who could prick you without saying a word.

blocks.text: Elder Mottled Boar
Levels 8–9, pale-coated. It returns to a light coat, as though bleached by the sun. That’s my poetic explanation, not a physician’s diagnosis. Age grants it no new rank of ability.
Corrupted Mottled Boar

Levels 10–11, black-coated. Despite its troubling name, it remains a tameable beast. Don’t confuse it with the Helboar of the Blasted Lands: there, the word “demon” has a very practical meaning for a hunter.
On the plains, I discovered that boars are called up for service, too. Judging by their behavior, their pay comes in carrots and opportunities to headbutt passersby.
Battleboar

Levels 3–4, golden-coated. It lives near the quilboar territory in Mulgore. It can be tamed and knows Charge, Rank 1. A local tauren assignment calls for the snout and flank of Battleboars: these are quest items, not a promise of some new recipe for your cookbook.

blocks.alt: A golden and a reddish battleboar press their snouts together; a wooden practice spear lies nearby.
blocks.caption: Drill practice: step forward, grunt, forget the order.

blocks.text: Bristleback Battleboar

Levels 4–5, red-coated. It keeps farther inside the Bristleback tribe’s territory in Razorfen Kraul. It can be tamed and knows the same first rank. Its masters’ military discipline does not make it untamable—just choose your meeting place carefully.

If you see a quilboar with a spear on the hill, don’t add it to this chapter. It’s already busy taking inventory of your belongings. I once lost a pencil that way and gained a healthy respect for keeping my distance.

chapters.title: Razorfen Kraul: A Boar in Armor

blocks.text: I went in with companions. They called it a loot run; I called it a scientific expedition. Both descriptions appeared on the repair bill. The three Agam’ar listed below are elite beasts that can be tamed; each knows Charge, Rank 3.
Agam’ar

Levels 24–25. A brown boar in rough harness. Its armor gives the companion a distinctive look, but offers no special advantage over an equally trained relative. Still, standing beside it makes me look like an organized army.
Raging Agam’ar

Levels 25–26. Pale-coated and harnessed. A fine alternative if you’ve been staring too long at the enormous master of the pen: find your pale armored companion here instead of trying to lead the boss away by the nose.

blocks.alt: Three Razorfen Kraul boars: brown, black, and pale, fitted with rough straps and metal plates.
blocks.caption: They tried on the armor without my assistance. Wise of them: I’m a worse tailor than I am a runner.

blocks.text: Rotting Agam’ar

Level 28. A black-coated boar in harness. The name is grim, but this is a tameable beast, not a separate school of necromancy. It differs in both appearance and habitat from the Plagued Swine of the Eastern Plaguelands.
Three Encounters That Won’t Become Friendships

Agathelos the Raging is the elite master of the pen, level 33; he cannot be tamed. He can drop Ferine Leggings and the boar-tusk-sharpening dagger. The Boar Spirit is an elite ghostly visitor, levels 16–20, and is not suitable as a pet either. The Tamed Battleboar, levels 22–26, already serves the local masters, so don’t count on it as a reliable taming target. If you’re after a companion, choose one of the three Agam’ar above.

chapters.title: The Blasted Lands: Boars with a Bad Reputation

blocks.text: Here, I stopped being able to tell dust from seasoning. I had to put away the cooking pot. My hunter’s journal, however, gained two remarkable teachers and one very convincing mistake of nature.
Ashmane Boar

Levels 48–49, red-coated, tameable. It teaches Charge, Rank 5. The wild beast’s bluish haze disappears after taming, so don’t pay a guide who promises you a permanent fog. I did. Now I have a very precise note about the phenomenon.
Grunter

A rare level-50 beast. It can be tamed and knows Charge, Rank 5, and Dash, Rank 3. It’s worth seeking out in these lands for the encounter and the training, but its black coat is no rarer than that of some boars in Dun Morogh. A rare acquaintance does not necessarily come in a rare color.

blocks.alt: Black Grunter and a red Ashmane Boar in profile among several dry branches.
blocks.caption: You recognize rarity by the encounter, not by the color of the bristles.

blocks.text: Helboar

Levels 52–53. A boar in appearance, a demon by nature. It cannot be tamed; bread will not correct this mistake. It stayed outside the list of companions in my sketchbook, but left a very tangible hole in my boot.

Ashmane Boars, Grunter, and Helboars provide the lightweight hides needed for the errands of the blood mages in these lands. Useful materials for their mixtures—not an invitation to make soup. I wrote that in large letters, because my cooking journal was lying much too close by.

chapters.title: The Eastern Plaguelands: The Last Teacher

blocks.text: Plagued Swine

Level 60. Among the ruins in the northwestern Eastern Plaguelands, you may find a beast whose hide looks sickly and eaten away by disease. For all its appearance, it is still an animal—and it can be tamed. Its unusual plague-ridden look accompanies the highest rank of Charge found in these lands: Rank 6.

blocks.alt: Side sketch of a plague boar: sparse bristles, a sickly green-gray hide, and prominent ribs; dry leaves lie nearby.
blocks.caption: I dried this page by the fire in silence.

blocks.text: I sat nearby for a long time, sketching its flank. For the first time on the whole journey, I didn’t feel like inventing a nickname. The land around it had been ravaged, yet the beast still searched beneath a stone for a root—a common bit of boar business that had survived an uncommon disaster.

If you take such a companion, don’t expect its dreadful hide to grant secret powers. But you can learn the required rank of the ability and pass it on to your old boar. You needn’t replace your familiar grunting friend every time you meet a new teacher.

chapters.title: A Hunter’s Reminder, Written on a Surviving Map

blocks.text: Boars eat meat, fish, bread, cheese, fruit, and mushrooms. In short, nearly everything I’d planned to eat myself. Keep an eye on your companion’s happiness and loyalty; food that is too weak for its level will please it less. Ale is not on the list, a fact for which my provisions are grateful.

Charge briefly immobilizes a target and empowers the next attack. It is not a stun. Dash helps you run faster; Bite lets you spend the rest of your fighting spirit. These abilities must be learned separately: having tusks is no substitute for a lesson.

blocks.alt: A black boar charges toward a crooked straw target; several strokes suggest motion.
blocks.caption: The target had no objections. Perhaps it didn’t have time.

items: Leave your regular companion in the stable, make room at your side, and tame a beast that knows the ability you need. Its level must not exceed your own.
Let the new beast use the ability until you learn it yourself. Taming alone is not enough.
Call back your former companion and teach it through Beast Training. The appropriate level and training points are required.

rows.label: Charge II
rows.value: Goretusks and older Mountain Boars; pet level 12 or higher.

rows.label: Charge III
rows.value: Bellygrub and the Agam’ar; pet level 24 or higher.

rows.label: Charge IV
rows.value: No known teacher has been found in these lands.

rows.label: Charge V
rows.value: Ashmane Boar or Grunter; pet level 48 or higher.

blocks.text: I searched for the missing fourth-rank teacher longer than I searched for my own tankard. The tankard turned up. The teacher did not. Don’t repeat my expedition solely for its sake.

chapters.title: Five Notes Beside the Cooking Pot

blocks.text: A living boar’s appearance and the hide removed by a skinner are two different things. A pale coat does not promise pale leather, and a rare name does not mean rare materials. If someone offers you “Grunter’s unique hide,” check first that they aren’t just selling you a story.

blocks.alt: A living brown boar gazes hopefully at a cooking pot, a ladle, and a whole apple.
blocks.caption: The chief taster demands an apple before the trials begin.

rows.label: Roasted Boar Meat
rows.value: Cooking 1. One piece of boar meat; a simple recipe learned from a trainer.

rows.label: Beer-Basted Boar Ribs
rows.value: Cooking 25. One Crag Boar rib and one mug of chatty ale. The recipe is associated with Ragnar Thunderbrew in Kharanos.

rows.label: Goretusk Liver Pie
rows.value: Cooking 50. One liver and one herb-baked egg. The recipe can be bought from Kendor Kabonka in Stormwind.

rows.label: Westfall Stew
rows.value: Cooking 75. One Goretusk snout, one Murloc eye, and one tough condor meat. Kendor sells this recipe, too.

rows.label: Crispy Boar Ribs
rows.value: Cooking 80. One boar rib and one herb-baked egg; the recipe comes from a trainer.

blocks.text: For Ragnar’s actual quest, you need six ribs and one ale; for a single serving made from the learned recipe, you need one rib and one ale. I mixed those up exactly once. It was a very wet dish.

Beer-Basted Boar Ribs grant 2 Stamina and 2 Spirit; Goretusk Liver Pie and Crispy Boar Ribs grant 4. The bonus lasts 15 minutes, provided you sit and eat for at least 10 seconds. Roasted Boar Meat and Westfall Stew, among these five, only restore health. Not every meal is a blessing; some are simply meals.

chapters.title: The Return: The Last Page Smells of Apples

blocks.text: I returned to Kharanos with a torn map, an armful of drawings, and knowledge no sensible innkeeper would trade for a discount: boars have far more in common with dwarves than we care to admit. Both enjoy a hearty meal, curse a bad road, and consider a wall an insufficient argument.

If you need a companion, choose one you’ll be glad to return to after a hard day. You can visit a trainer for an ability. You can travel to another land for a different coat. But that familiar, contented grunt beside the campfire is something no trainer can teach.

blocks.alt: A black boar sleeps curled up beside a pair of worn dwarf boots; an apple lies between them.
blocks.caption: Until the next road. Leave the apple for the guard.

blocks.text: I swear it by my beard: this is a scientific conclusion. The signature below is a little smudged because my co-author was testing whether ink is edible.
Dur Blackbeard, Dwarf. Written in my own hand; approved by one boar and disapproved by the owner of a pumpkin patch.
